extracted.intended_audience: federal agency policymakers, regulatory policy officers, OMB/OIRA staff, and other executive-branch officials involved in drafting or reviewing federal regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and quality standards for developing, reviewing, and publishing executive-branch federal regulations and significant guidance under Executive Order 12866. Covers agency obligations, OIRA review, planning, transparency, and analytic requirements (costs/benefits, alternatives, risk assessment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory philosophy (overall standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should promulgate only such regulations as are required by law, are necessary to interpret the law, or are made necessary by compelling public need; agencies should assess all costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives (including the alternative of not regulating) and select approaches that maximize net benefits, unless a statute requires another approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs and benefits include quantifiable measures (to the fullest extent usefully estimated) and qualitative measures difficult to quantify but essential to consider; consideration should include economic, environmental, public health and safety, distributive impacts, and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 1 — identify specific market failure or problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify in writing the specific market failure (such as externalities, market power, lack of information) or other specific problem that it intends to address and assess the significance of that problem to enable assessment of whether any new regulation is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a written statement of the problem and its significance to justify regulatory intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 2 — examine whether existing law/regulations contributed to problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall examine whether existing regulations (or other law) have created, or contributed to, the problem that a new regulation is intended to correct and whether those regulations (or other law) should be modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider modification of existing legal instruments before adopting new regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3 — assess nonregulatory alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify and assess available alternatives to direct regulation, including providing economic incentives (e.g., user fees, marketable permits) or providing information upon which choices can be made by the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically consider incentive-based and informational approaches as potential substitutes for prescriptive regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 4 — consider risk prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: In setting regulatory priorities, each agency shall consider, to the extent reasonable, the degree and nature of the risks posed by various substances or activities within its jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparative risk considerations to inform priorities among potential regulatory actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 5 — design cost-effective regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency determines regulation is the best available method, it shall design its regulations in the most cost-effective manner to achieve the regulatory objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider incentives for innovation, consistency, predictability, enforcement and compliance costs (to government, regulated entities, and the public), flexibility, distributive impacts, and equity when designing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 6 — reasoned determination that benefits justify costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall assess both the costs and the benefits of the intended regulation and, recognizing that some costs and benefits are difficult to quantify, propose or adopt a regulation only upon a reasoned determination that the benefits justify its costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must record a reasoned judgment balancing costs and benefits before adopting regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 7 — rely on best reasonably obtainable information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall base its decisions on the best reasonably obtainable scientific, technical, economic, and other information concerning the need for, and consequences of, the intended regulation or guidance document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the information sources and basis for regulatory conclusions; use appropriate expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 8 — prefer performance objectives when feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify and assess alternative forms of regulation and, to the extent feasible, specify performance objectives, rather than specifying the behavior or manner of compliance that regulated entities must adopt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible define outcomes/performance targets rather than prescriptive methods to allow flexibility and innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 9 — consult state, local, and tribal officials and minimize unique burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever feasible, agencies shall seek views of appropriate State, local, and tribal officials before imposing regulatory requirements that might significantly or uniquely affect those governmental entities; agencies shall assess effects on these governments and seek to minimize uniquely burdensome mandates and harmonize Federal actions with related state/local/tribal functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess resource availability for compliance at subfederal levels and pursue harmonization and minimization of unique burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 10 — avoid inconsistent, incompatible, duplicative rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall avoid regulations and guidance documents that are inconsistent, incompatible, or duplicative with its other regulations and guidance or those of other Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen for inter-agency conflicts and duplications during rule development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 11 — tailor to impose least burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall tailor its regulations and guidance documents to impose the least burden on society, including individuals, businesses of differing sizes, and other entities, consistent with obtaining regulatory objectives, taking into account the costs of cumulative regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider differential impacts (e.g., small communities, small businesses) and cumulative regulatory costs when tailoring requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 12 — draft in simple, understandable language
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall draft its regulations and guidance documents to be simple and easy to understand, with the goal of minimizing potential uncertainty and litigation arising from such uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language practices to reduce ambiguity and legal challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'Regulation' (scope and exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation means an agency statement of general applicability and future effect designed to implement, interpret, or prescribe law or policy or to describe procedure or practice requirements; it does not include: (1) regulations issued under formal rulemaking provisions of 5 U.S.C. 556, 557; (2) regulations pertaining to military or foreign affairs (with limited exceptions); (3) regulations limited to agency organization, management, or personnel matters; or (4) other categories exempted by the Administrator of OIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine whether a document counts as a regulation subject to EO 12866 review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'Regulatory action'
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory action means any substantive action by an agency (normally published in the Federal Register) that promulgates or is expected to lead to promulgation of a final regulation, including notices of inquiry, advance notices of proposed rulemaking, and notices of proposed rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers the procedures and review obligations in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'Significant regulatory action' (threshold criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: A significant regulatory action is any regulatory action likely to result in a regulation that may: (1) have an annual effect on the economy of $100 million or more or adversely affect in a material way the economy, a sector, productivity, competition, jobs, the environment, public health or safety, or State/local/tribal governments or communities; (2) create a serious inconsistency or interfere with another agency's action; (3) materially alter budgetary impacts of entitlements/grants/user fees/loan programs or rights/obligations; or (4) raise novel legal or policy issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these criteria to determine whether enhanced analytic and OIRA review requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'Guidance document' and 'Significant guidance document'
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance document: agency statement of general applicability and future effect other than a regulatory action that sets forth policy or interpretation. Significant guidance document: one that may reasonably be anticipated to (A) lead to an annual effect of $100 million or more or materially adverse effects; (B) create serious inconsistency with another agency; (C) materially alter budgetary impacts; or (D) raise novel legal or policy issues; with specified exclusions (parallel to regulation exclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant guidance documents are subject to advance notification and possible OIRA consultation analogous to significant regulatory actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified Regulatory Agenda and Regulatory Plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall prepare an agenda of all regulations under development or review and, beginning in 1994, a Regulatory Plan of the most important significant regulatory actions the agency reasonably expects to issue, containing specified minimum elements (A-F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory Plan must include: (A) statement of regulatory objectives/priorities and relation to President's priorities; (B) summary of each planned significant action including alternatives and preliminary cost/benefit estimates and combined aggregate estimates; (C) summary of legal basis with citations; (D) statement of need and risk-reduction explanation; (E) schedule including statutory/judicial deadlines; (F) contact info for public; Plans forwarded to OIRA by June 1 and published annually in October Unified Regulatory Agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning mechanism — coordination, circulation, and conflict identification
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA circulates agency Plans to affected agencies and Advisors within 10 calendar days; agencies and OIRA must notify each other of potential conflicts, and the Director may consult with agency heads and request further coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should promptly notify OIRA and other agencies where conflicts are suspected; agencies may comment on other Plans with a copy to OIRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Working Group (establishment and role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator of OIRA shall convene a Regulatory Working Group of agency representatives and Advisors to assist in identifying and analyzing important regulatory issues, develop innovative techniques, evaluate comparative risk assessment, and develop streamlined approaches for small businesses; the group meets at least quarterly and may commission analytical studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working Group serves as inter-agency forum and resource for methodological innovations and cross-cutting analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing regulations review program (90-day submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 90 days each agency shall submit to OIRA a program under which the agency will periodically review its existing significant regulations to determine whether any should be modified or eliminated; any significant regulations selected for review shall be included in the agency's annual Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program should be consistent with agency resources and priorities; agencies should identify legislative mandates that require continuation of regulations believed unnecessary or outdated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibility — public participation and comment periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide the public with meaningful participation in the regulatory process, and before issuing an NPRM should, where appropriate, seek involvement of beneficiaries and those expected to be burdened; in most cases the agency should provide a comment period of not less than 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider formal rulemaking under 5 U.S.C. 556 and 557 for complex determinations and explore consensual mechanisms (e.g., negotiated rulemaking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibility — designate Regulatory Policy Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days each agency head shall designate one Presidential Appointee as Regulatory Policy Officer, advise OMB of the designation, and annually update OMB; the officer shall be involved at each stage of the regulatory process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory Policy Officer fosters development of effective, innovative, least-burdensome regulations and ensures compliance with EO principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency reporting to OIRA for significant regulatory actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For matters identified as significant (or determined by OIRA to be significant), the issuing agency shall provide OIRA the draft text, a reasonably detailed description of the need for the action and how it will meet that need, and an assessment of potential costs and benefits and consistency with statutory mandates and the President's priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must explain how the action avoids undue interference with State/local/tribal governments and provide information in the manner specified by OIRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced analytic requirements for high-impact significant actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For significant regulatory actions within the scope of the $100M (3(f)(1)) criterion, the agency must also provide: (i) an assessment and underlying analysis of anticipated benefits with quantification to the extent feasible; (ii) an assessment and underlying analysis of anticipated costs with quantification to the extent feasible; and (iii) an assessment and underlying analysis of costs and benefits of potentially effective and reasonably feasible alternatives and explanation why the planned action is preferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require underlying analysis and attempt quantification where feasible; include consideration of improvements to current regulation and viable nonregulatory actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency and statutory-deadline exceptions and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: In emergency situations or when an agency is legally obligated to act more quickly than normal review procedures allow, the agency shall notify OIRA as soon as possible and, to the extent practicable, comply with submission and analytic requirements; for actions governed by statutory or court-imposed deadlines agencies should schedule to permit sufficient time for OIRA review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When practicable agencies should still provide the information in subsections (a)(3)(B) and (C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication transparency by agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication or issuance, the agency shall: (i) make available to the public the information submitted to OIRA (a)(3)(B) and (C); (ii) identify in a complete, clear, and simple manner the substantive changes between the draft submitted to OIRA and the action announced; and (iii) identify changes made at the suggestion or recommendation of OIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All information provided to the public shall be in plain, understandable language.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA review scope and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA may review only actions identified by the agency or by OIRA as significant. OIRA shall waive review or notify the agency in writing of results within: (A) 10 working days for preliminary regulatory actions prior to an NPRM; (B) 90 calendar days for all other regulatory actions after submission of required information (or 45 days if previously reviewed and no material change). The review may be extended once by no more than 30 calendar days with Director approval and at agency head request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should plan timelines to accommodate OIRA review windows; extensions possible under specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA return and explanation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If OIRA returns a regulatory action to an agency for further consideration of some or all provisions, the Administrator shall provide a written explanation setting forth the pertinent provision of the Executive order on which OIRA is relying; the agency head may disagree in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written record must identify the EO basis for returns; agencies may document disagreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA disclosure and communications rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the Administrator of OIRA (or a particular designee) shall receive oral communications initiated by persons not employed by the executive branch regarding the substance of a regulatory action under review. All substantive communications between OIRA personnel and outside persons shall: (i) invite a representative from the issuing agency to meetings; (ii) have OIRA forward to the issuing agency, within 10 working days, all written communications and the dates/names of individuals in substantive oral communications; and (iii) be publicly disclosed as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure agency participation in communications; forward and log communications promptly for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA public log requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA shall maintain a publicly available log containing at minimum: (i) status of all regulatory actions (including if/when/by whom Presidential consideration was requested); (ii) a notation of all written communications forwarded to issuing agencies; and (iii) dates and names of individuals involved in all substantive oral communications and subject matter discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log is a central transparency tool for OIRA interactions during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA disclosure of exchanged documents after action
rubrics_metrics.description: After the regulatory action has been published or after the agency announces its decision not to publish, OIRA shall make available to the public all documents exchanged between OIRA and the agency during the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates public accountability for OIRA influence on rule content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language requirement for OIRA communications
rubrics_metrics.description: All information provided to the public by OIRA shall be in plain, understandable language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply clear-writing standards to disclosure materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of conflicts — Presidential review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Disagreements between agency heads or between OMB and any agency that cannot be resolved by the Administrator of OIRA shall be resolved by the President with assistance of the Chief of Staff; Presidential consideration may be initiated only by the Director, the issuing agency head, or a head of an agency with significant interest; recommendations shall be developed within 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications with outside persons during Presidential review must be in writing and forwarded to affected agencies for inclusion in public dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication restriction pending OIRA review
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as required by law, an agency shall not publish or otherwise issue any regulatory action subject to section 6 review until (1) OIRA notifies the agency that it has waived review or completed its review without requests for further consideration, or (2) the applicable time period expires without OIRA returning the action; to publish earlier an agency may request Presidential consideration through the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule prevents premature publication before centralized review completes or waives review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant guidance document notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide OIRA advance notification of any significant guidance documents and, upon OIRA request, provide the content of the draft guidance with a brief explanation of need and how it will meet that need; OIRA may require additional consultation before issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat significant guidance analogously to significant regulations for advance review and consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency duty to publish Plan and solicit views
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans developed by the issuing agency shall be published in the October Unified Regulatory Agenda and made available to Congress, state/local/tribal governments, and the public; any views on agency Plans should be directed to the issuing agency with a copy to OIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use published Plans as the vehicle for public and intergovernmental feedback on upcoming regulatory priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to identify legislative mandates possibly needing reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director, in consultation with Advisors, may identify for review existing regulations or groups of regulations that affect a particular group/industry/sector or may identify legislative mandates that may be appropriate for reconsideration by Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and Advisors should flag statutory requirements that may warrant legislative review when they appear obsolete or burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of agency authority and judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Order shall be construed to impair or affect authority vested by law in an agency or the head thereof, including the Attorney General's authority relating to litigation; nothing in the Order affects otherwise available judicial review of agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EO 12866 is intended to improve internal management and does not create enforceable private rights.
